Upstream GCC commit 5d419c69ce2e6b86d7da75f18736904885674219 (PR libstdc++/124370) stops std::bitset wide-character stream extraction from sizing its buffer without sizeof(wchar_t). The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie, re-expressed against the 14.2.0 operator>>. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-115455

Upstream GCC commit 2fd8866591b5aea7098835f80ab7e176382175ae makes std::vector<bool> constructors check the element count against max_size() before sizing the bit array, so the word count cannot wrap. The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie, without the from_range constructor hunk, which GCC 14.2.0 does not have. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-114691

CVE-2026-85747 (GHSA-685w-q87j-wqw3) is a missing digest check in the github.com/docker/distribution registry client: manifests and blobs fetched by digest were returned without being hashed, so a malicious registry could substitute content. docker/distribution v2.8.3 has no fixed release; the fix shipped in distribution v3.1.2 as commits https://github.com/distribution/distribution/commit/8f91c26c8888a95a36c2357a6e30bc15d4dd76d3 (manifests) and https://github.com/distribution/distribution/commit/93c6e1a3b3c874a73fbd6b8fa9b37577223cff9e (blobs). The docker packages listed here apply both changes to the registry client vendored in Moby, so dockerd rejects manifest and blob content that does not match the requested digest. The module version reported by go version -m stays v2.8.3+incompatible because the fix is applied to vendored source. Advisory: https://github.com/distribution/distribution/security/advisories/GHSA-685w-q87j-wqw3

CVE-2026-85747 (GHSA-685w-q87j-wqw3) is fixed in github.com/distribution/distribution v3.1.2 by validating manifest bodies against digest-pinned requests in registry/client.(*manifests).Get. The cdi-uploadserver binary links github.com/docker/distribution v2.8.3+incompatible only as a transitive dependency of github.com/containers/image/v5/docker, which imports registry/api and registry/client/auth/challenge but not registry/client manifests. A go list -deps build of cmd/cdi-uploadserver at containerized-data-importer v1.66.1 does not include github.com/docker/distribution/registry/client, and the built binary has no manifests.Get symbol. The upload server serves HTTPS uploads and does not act as a distribution registry client performing digest-pinned manifest fetches, so the vulnerable code is not compiled into this artifact.

CVE-2026-56392 is an integer overflow in unexpand buffer allocation that multiplies max_column_width by MB_LEN_MAX. That allocation path was introduced after coreutils 9.7 (multibyte expand/unexpand support; first present in 9.11). Debian trixie and this DHI package ship 9.7, which still allocates with ximalloc(max_column_width) and does not contain the vulnerable multiply.

statements.action_statement: Use-after-free in xmlParseInternalSubset (DoS via crafted XML with improper entity resolution) affecting libxml2 2.9.11-2.11.0. The DHI package ships the Debian trixie 2.9.14 repack, which is in the affected range. Upstream fixed this only as a side effect of the entity-amplification rework in https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/commit/463bbeeca1805b5c4828f50d0fefc4eebaf620df (v2.11.0): a large parser.c rewrite plus ABI-changing additions to the public entities.h and parser.h structures. There is no isolated upstream patch, and neither Debian nor Ubuntu ships a backport to their 2.9.x branches. The fix cannot be applied to the 2.9.14 source without breaking API/ABI version compatibility for consumers, so no patch is carried. Reference: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-6653

Uncontrolled recursion in xmlParseSGMLCatalog reachable only when a local user parses an untrusted SGML catalog with the xmlcatalog CLI. Both Debian (unimportant) and upstream consider this negligible (using untrusted SGML catalogs makes no sense). The upstream recursion-depth fix targets libxml2 2.15 catalog.c and does not apply to the trixie 2.9.14 source without invasive multi-function changes for a negligible CLI-only issue. Reference: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2025-8732
